messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test `testArDelete()` tries to "delete" an entry from an Ar archive by copying all entries except one from an input Ar archive (bla.ar) to a new output Ar archive (bla2.ar). The test asserts that exactly one entry was "deleted". The problem described in the bug report is that after "deletion," the command line tool for Ar archives still shows both entries (test1.xml and test2.xml) in the old archive file, implying the deletion is not reflected in the original file.

The test code itself looks correct: it creates an archive with two files, then creates a new archive by copying only one file and counting the deleted ones.

The ArArchiveInputStream.getNextEntry() delegates to getNextArEntry() which reads an entry from input stream by interpreting the ar archive format headers. It reads bytes for the entry name, length, etc., performs header validation, then creates an ArArchiveEntry with the name and length.

The ArArchiveOutputStream.putArchiveEntry() writes headers for the given entry, ensuring the archive header is written for the first entry and closing previous entries properly. The closeArchiveEntry() ensures padding if needed.

However, the core issue is the misunderstanding that "deletion" modifies the original archive. In reality, the test creates a new output file (bla2.ar) excluding one entry, but the original file (bla.ar) remains unchanged. The bug report says that checking `ar -t bla.ar` still lists the deleted file because the original archive was not modified or replaced by the new archive after deletion.

The test does not check the contents of bla2.ar but blames deletion behavior on the original file. The original file is never modified or deleted/replaced in the test.

Hence, there's no bug in the archive stream handling, but rather the deletion workflow is incomplete: the modified archive should replace the original on disk to reflect the deletion. The getNextEntry behavior is correct as it only reads the new archive and excludes the deleted file.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this Ar archive deletion behavior.

In summary, the deletion "looks" successful in the new archive, but the original archive is not replaced, causing confusion.

The test expects deletion in-place, but the code creates a new archive file without replacing the old one.

This is an issue of usage pattern or expected behavior, not a bug in the code reading or writing the archive format.

Possible improvement: document that deletion means creating a new archive and replacing the old file. Possibly provide helper methods for this.

Suggested fix locations would involve the test or code manipulating archives rather than the underlying ArArchiveInputStream or ArArchiveOutputStream.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
